items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Harry agreed to be the arranger... when we had worked out the details of my orchestra

ctx.x: Timmie Rosenkrantz, who had come to New York in 1933 and eventually became to be known as the "Barrel-House Baron", had married a Negro girl named Inez Cavanaugh whom I had known for quite a long time, and they opened a record shop on St. Nicholas Avenue near 147th Street. I started making the shop my hang-out and soon after that, Timmie asked me why I did not form an orchestra and he would manage it. I mentioned in this book before that Timmie was a real Danish Baron whom I had met at the Empire Ballroom in 1933…

Timmie was in the know as to what was happening in the jazz w world and knew the onwers of most of the clubs uptown and downtown So we talked about the band I should lead for a few days and then started to put the idea in action. Harry White, an ex-Cab Calloway trombonist, known as "Father" White, was also known as a fine arranger, but he had become an alchoholic victim, and was not in demand at the time. He started hanging out in Timmie's record shop also, and when we had worked out the details of my orchestra,…

We contacted a pianist named General Morgan and his first name really was General. He was a fine pianist. Arthur Herbert, who was an Ex-Coleman Hawkins drummer, Franz Jackson, a tenor man and Herb Fleming on trombone are the only known members of the orchestra that I can remember. "Father" White was living in a back room of the record shop and Timmie was feeding him and also gave him a little drinking money. The shop wasn't doing too well, so not much money was coming in, and we musicians weren't working, so we…
